name: Yaesu FT-2800M
notes: Stock, unmodified US FT-2800M: a single-band 2 m FM mobile (~2003), 65/25/10/5 W. Unlike the FT-270R/FT-277R handhelds, this one reports its own name, so the CHIRP driver is chirp/drivers/ft2800.py (VENDOR 'Yaesu', MODEL 'FT-2800M') and no VX-model aliasing is involved. Bench-verified 2026-09-14 by a read-only clone download from a physical radio: it identified as 'Yaesu FT-2800M', sent the USA-unmodified ID block 0c 01 41 33 35 02 00 b8, and produced a 7905-byte file (7680 bytes of codeplug plus CHIRP's 225-byte metadata trailer), all through a Prolific PL2303 cable at 9600 baud. The image held 177 occupied memories, all FM, longest name exactly 6 characters, charset upper-case alphanumeric plus '?'. 47 of those memories sit outside 144-148 MHz (public-safety and marine VHF up to 161.52 MHz); that is receive-only scanner use and is NOT evidence of a transmit mod, which is precisely why the wider span below is recorded as rx_only. Storage limits are the driver's: max_channels 200 is memory_bounds (0, 199) and the memory[200] struct, matching the published 200-memory figure; max_channel_name_chars 6 is names[200] with char name[6]. Those six-character tags are as tight as the FT-270R's, so display names need aggressive shortening, and CHARSET is upper-case alphanumeric plus ()+-=*/|_ only. modes is ["FM"]: valid_modes is ["FM", "NFM"] with no AM, and bandwidths_khz 12.5/25 follows that split. The TX band is the US amateur 2 m allocation 144-148 MHz; the driver's single valid_bands entry 137-174 MHz is the programming path's span, recorded here as rx_only because stock firmware will not transmit outside the ham band. That is confirmed over the air, not just inferred: the bench radio was keyed outside 144-148 on 2026-09-14 and would not transmit, which agrees with the stock clone ID block it reports. A radio with the extended-TX mod is a separate id, yaesu_ft2800m_mars, and the two are told apart by the clone ID block, not by the reported model string, which is 'Yaesu FT-2800M' either way. max_zones is 1 as a profile-0.1 compatibility shim: the driver sets has_bank = False. Clone protocol is the 7680-byte FT-2800 format at 9600 baud with even parity, transferred in 32-byte blocks; clone mode is manual on every transfer (hold MHz + Low + D/MR while powering on, then MHz to send / Low to receive). WRITE PATH: both the CHIRP.app GUI and the headless chirp-writer backend are bench-verified on a physical radio, 2026-09-14. HEADLESS READ: a chirp-writer read reproduced the intended codeplug with zero mismatches across all 200 memory and name slots, only two bytes outside those regions differed (0x1559 and 0x1577, radio-maintained state such as current channel), and the channels were still on the front panel afterwards, so a completed read changes nothing. HEADLESS WRITE: confirmed twice in opposite directions, with a deliberately distinguishable payload each way so that a no-op could not be mistaken for a success. Writing a 177-channel codeplug over a 20-channel one put the expected channels at the expected memory slots on the radio's own display, and writing the 20-channel one back reversed it; independently, each run's mandatory pre-write backup captured exactly what the previous run had left, which confirms the sequence without relying on the display at all. Run the write with --read-back omitted when the operator cannot reliably arm a third clone cycle. EARLIER CLEARINGS EXPLAINED: twice the radio was found at a single default 144.000 MHz channel, which was at first misread as a failed write. The cause was pressing Low during a read-back attempt. Low arms the radio to RECEIVE a clone, which clears memory first, so a receive that is armed and never completed empties the radio. MHz sends, Low receives: on a read press MHz only, on the upload leg press Low. Ordering also differs by leg -- for a read, arm the host first and then press MHz inside its roughly 30-second listen window (pressing MHz before the host opens the port shows ERROR on the radio), whereas for an upload the radio must be armed with Low before the host starts sending. Keep the pre-write backup regardless: one stray keypress empties this radio, so its own contents are never the only copy.
